messages:
mira: quick heads-up — did a focused bring-up for agora-embed (int6) against our multilingual holdout. noticing a drop concentrated in zh R@10 while en/es look fine. attaching quick run notes.
mira: command used:
```
./embed_bench --model=agora-int6 --dataset=multilang_holdout_3k --langs=en,es,zh --k=1,5,10 --quant=per-tensor --whiten=trained_on_en_es --batch=256
```
dave: paste numbers please, small thread :slightly_smiling_face:
mira: table (avg of 4 runs):
```
model         lang  R@1    R@5    R@10
agora-fp16    zh    0.398  0.717  0.785
agora-int6    zh    0.392  0.703  0.741  <-- delta -0.044 at R@10
agora-fp16    en    0.462  0.773  0.831
agora-int6    en    0.459  0.768  0.828
agora-fp16    es    0.441  0.754  0.812
agora-int6    es    0.438  0.751  0.809
```
olga: interesting that R@1/R@5 less affected. could be whitening mismatch or quant tails. did you use same normalization/whitening pipeline?
mira: yes: L2 norm then PCA-whiten. but whiten matrix trained on en+es dev set (we excluded zh historically).
dave: possible domain shift. quant adds noise -> with whitening not representing zh manifold some vectors wander across cluster boundaries at larger k. can you run whitening retrain including zh samples?
mira: started that run (6189990300). ETA ~6m.
bench-bot: run 6189990300 completed. agora-int6 with zh-in-whiten: R@10 zh = 0.768 (was 0.741). partial recovery. artifacts: /artifacts/6189990300/meta.json
mira: OK that recovers ~60% of the gap. next, I pulled norm stats pre/post quant:
```
metric      model       lang  mean_norm  std_norm
L2_norm     agora-fp16  zh    11.8       1.9
L2_norm     agora-int6  zh    11.3       3.6   <-- heavier tail
L2_norm     agora-fp16  en    12.4       2.0
L2_norm     agora-int6  en    12.3       2.1
```
olga: heavier std on int6-zh suggests outliers. try per-channel quant and/or stratified calibration sampling biased to tail lexemes.
mira: queued two quick jobs: per-channel int6 and stratified-calib per-tensor int6. runs 6189990451 and 6189990452.
bench-bot: run 6189990451 (per-channel) done: agora-int6-perchannel zh R@10 = 0.780 mean_norm=11.9 std=2.2
bench-bot: run 6189990452 (stratified-calib) done: agora-int6-stratcalib zh R@10 = 0.775 mean_norm=11.6 std=2.4
dave: per-channel looks best. stratified helps but per-channel + zh-in-whiten likely best combo. can you try combo?
mira: queued per-channel + zh-whiten (6189990520).
bench-bot: run 6189990520 finished: agora-int6-perchan-zhwhiten R@10 zh = 0.789 (near fp16 0.785). logs: /bench/6189990520/log.txt
olga: great. conclusion: two interacting factors — whitening sample coverage and quant granularity. recommendations: (1) require whitening training to include all target languages or validate per-lang drift, (2) prefer per-channel quant for multilingual models with tail mass, (3) add a microbench to onboarding that reports per-lang R@k and L2 norm distribution and top1-top2 cosine gap.
dave: also propose automated canary: fail int6 builds if any language R@10 drops > 0.03 vs fp16 baseline. open PR?
mira: will open PR updating model-onboard checklist, add bench flags, and include a short note in model card re: whitening sampling. filing ticket EMBED-ONB-3512 with runs and artifacts.
olga: thanks team — good quick detective loop :thumbsup:
